# GitHub envelope source captures

These item objects were exported on **2026-10-11** from the live production
Plexus store by the operator, from public `cortexkit` repositories only.
Whitespace was expanded for review. The captures have since been anonymized:
human names, logins, emails, account IDs, encoded account node IDs and URLs
embedding those identities were replaced consistently with fictional values.
Issue/PR titles and bodies, CI display titles and commit messages, and release
prose are invented. Human email addresses use `example.com`, except fictional
GitHub noreply addresses that retain the ID+login form needed for attribution.
External service bots also have fictional logins/IDs, retaining their `[bot]`
suffix and `Bot` type. Plexus product bots and the organization retain their
names and types. Every
field and type, null, timestamp, repository ID, number, commit SHA, job/run ID
and conclusion is preserved. These are no longer unmodified captures.

- `webhook_*.json`: captured item objects stored from real relay deliveries
  (`body.issue`, `body.pull_request`, `body.workflow_job`, `body.workflow_run`).
  The issue-shaped object is GitHub's issue representation of a PR conversation.
- `poll_*.json`: captured polled items. `poll_issue.json` is the MCP shape with
  uppercase `OPEN`, no `html_url`, and only a login in its user object.
- `poll_release.json`: a real polled release. The deployed GitHub App does not
  receive release events: Contents permission is deliberately disabled.

Plexus's v1 store saves the item, not its delivery wrapper. Golden tests construct
and explicitly name a **constructed wrapper around a captured item** containing
`action`, `sender` and `repository`; those wrapper fields are not captures.
The expected envelopes are independent literal goldens, not generated by the
normalizer. The same-change test aligns the PR update timestamp between two
captures eight seconds apart to model a shared identity, without claiming the
captures themselves are the same delivery. Constructed comment metadata in that
test witnesses the allowed comment-field differences.

Envelope goldens inject `observed_at_ms` and expect `observed_at` as an RFC 3339
UTC string with millisecond precision. That timestamp is normalization metadata,
not a captured GitHub field: it records when the item first reached CortexKit
(relay receipt for webhooks, poll observation time for polling). Comparing it to
the activity time distinguishes a delivery delay from old news. Events stored
before this field was introduced remain byte-identical and lack `observed_at`;
the store regressions also pin their original digests.
